headline: Record revenue, adjusted profit up, but GAAP earnings slip
summary_short: Revenue rose 5.3% y/y to a record $6.66B and adjusted net income climbed over 20% to $569M, but GAAP net income fell 5.0% to $537M and diluted EPS fell 7.1% to $0.39 as the year-ago quarter included a $101M gain on ship sales that did not recur.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5.3% y/y to a record $6.66B on record net yields (constant currency) and $9.0B in customer deposits, but GAAP figures declined: operating income -8.8% to $852M, EBITDA -3.4% to $1.56B, net income -5.0% to $537M and diluted EPS -7.1% to $0.39, largely because the year-ago quarter benefited from a $101M gain on ship sales that this quarter lacks. Adjusted net income rose over 20% to $569M and adjusted EPS rose to $0.41, as cost discipline offset a nearly 30% jump in fuel prices. The company repurchased over $450M of stock under its buyback program and guided FY2026 to approximately 3.2% net-yield growth and $7.11B adjusted EBITDA; net debt to adjusted EBITDA improved to 3.1x.

drivers.explanation: CEO Josh Weinstein said cost efficiency and commercial execution delivered over 20% more to the bottom line despite geopolitical headwinds and nearly 30% higher fuel costs, exceeding March guidance by $100M.

Release attributes the record revenue to continued demand strength, record net yields (constant currency, +2.2%), 104% occupancy, and higher onboard/pre-cruise revenue alongside record customer deposits of $9.0B.
Gross margin yields fell 3.9% driven by higher fuel prices; adjusted cruise costs excluding fuel per ALBD held roughly flat on sharpened cost discipline, per the release.
Cruise costs per ALBD rose 6.0%, driven by higher fuel prices (up nearly 30%); a 5.6% improvement in fuel consumption per ALBD only partially offset the increase, per the release.
Same fuel-cost dynamic as operating income: quarterly fuel expense rose to $595M from $468M a year ago, per the income statement, while non-fuel cruise costs were held roughly flat.
Not explained in the release at this basis — the release only discusses its own non-GAAP 'adjusted EBITDA' (record $1.582B, up y/y), a different, non-comparable figure from this GAAP-basis metric.
Non-GAAP reconciliation shows the year-ago quarter included a $101M gain on ship sales and impairments that did not recur, plus a $73M ($0.06/share) unfavorable fuel/FX impact cited in the release.
Same $101M prior-year ship-sale gain and $73M fuel/FX headwind drove the GAAP EPS decline even as adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.41 from $0.35, per the release's own comparison.
Same driver as diluted EPS — absence of the year-ago $101M ship-sale gain plus the fuel/FX headwind; basic/diluted gap reflects convertible-note share dilution differences, not a separate cause.
Pretax income fell as operating income declined on fuel-cost pressure and the year-ago $101M ship-sale gain did not recur, partly offset by lower net interest expense ($285M vs $341M).
Shares outstanding edged down as the company's active buyback program — over $450M repurchased to date — reduced share count, per the capital-allocation section.
